title.narrative: Naturvårdsverket 2020-2024 Kapacitetsbyggnad för användning av miljödata
SEPA 2020-2024 Environmental Capacity Building on Data use

description.narrative:
Naturvårdsverket har inkommit med en ansökan till svenska ambassaden om finansiering på 9 miljoner kronor under tre år (2021-2023) för insatsen Environmental Capacity Building on Data Use. Insatsens kärna är kapacitetsutveckling på Kosovos naturvårdsmyndighet (KEPA) inom framförallt datahantering. Insatsen har tre tematiska fokusområden: luftföroreningar, klimatförändringar och vattenförvaltning. Kommunikation rörande miljöfrågor gentemot både beslutsfattare och en bredare allmänhet kommer att utgöra en väsentlig del av insatsen.
Det finns fyra specifika mål i insatsen 1) stärkt kommunikation; att tillhandahålla korrekt och omfattande miljödata till beslutsfattare och allmänheten, 2) förbättrade miljöinformationssystem; utveckla hantering och analys av miljödata, 3) kapacitetsutveckling för hållbar vattenhantering; stöd för att implementera flera av de planer som redan utvecklats för bättre vattenhantering och 4) stärkt kapacitet för miljöförbättringsåtgärder; utveckla användningen av analytiska verktyg som kostnadsnyttoanalyser och genomförbarhetsstudier på ett integrerat sätt när handlingsplaner, särskilt inom luftkvalitet och klimatförändringar, utvecklas.
Det övergripande målet med insatsen är att stärka den organisatoriska och individuella kapaciteten vid KEPA för att kunna arbeta i linje med riktlinjer från EU och på så sätt stödja Kosovo i arbetet för ett EU-närmande.
SEPA kommer att vara den enda avtalspartnern och det finns inga andra givare kopplade till insatsen.

The Swedish Environmental Protection Agency (SEPA) has applied to the Embassy for funding of SEK 9 million for three years (2021-2023) for the contribution Environmental Capacity Building on Data Use. The core of the contribution is capacity building on data management at the Kosovo Environmental Protection Agency (KEPA) with three thematic focus areas: air pollution, climate change and water management. Communication on environmental issues to both decision makers and the wider public is proposed to underpin the thematic areas and be a substantial part of the contribution.
There are four specific objectives of the contribution: 1) Strengthened communication; providing correct and comprehensive environmental data to decision makers and to the general public, 2) Improved environmental information systems; develop management and analysis of environmental data, 3) Capacity development for sustainable water management; support in implementing several of the plans already developed for better water management and 4) Strengthened implementation capacity for environmental quality improvement measures; using analytical tools such as cost benefit analysis and feasibility studies in an integrated manner when developing action plans, especially in the area of air quality and climate change.
The overall objective of the contribution is to strenghten organisational and individual capacity at KEPA to work in line with guidelines from the European Commission and that way support Kosovo towards EU accession.
SEPA will be the sole agreement partner and there are no other donors for the contribution.

The objective of the contribution is to support the Kosovo Environmental Protection Agency and the Ministry of Economy and Environment to build capacity in analyzing and making data available through the Environmental Information System (EIS) according to guidelines from the European Commission. This will prepare Kosovo to satisfy the requirements of Chapter 27 of the EU acquis, which is one prerequisite for EU accession. There are four specific objectives of the contribution: 1) Strengthened communication; providing correct and comprehensive environmental data to decision makers and to the general public, 2) Improved environmental information systems; develop management and analysis of environmental data, 3) Capacity development for sustainable water management; support in implementing several of the plans already developed for better water management and 4) Strengthened implementation capacity for environmental quality improvement measures; using analytical tools such as cost benefit analysis and feasibility studies in an integrated manner when developing action plans, especially in the area of air quality and climate change. The contribution will touch upon implementation of several of the EU directives connected to chapter 27, but especially the following ones: the Directive on Public Access to Environmental Information; the Directive on Establishing an Infrastructure for Spatial Information; the Water Framework Directive; the Groundwater Directive; and the Directive on Ambient Air Quality and Cleaner Air. Implementing an EU directive is normally an arduous process and involves several agencies and ministries. In other words, the contribution will not manage to implement specific directives per se, but rather ensure that KEPA is in a good position to play their part in the overall work needed to be carried out for implementation. The activities will center around several assessments of the current situation in the different areas and be followed up by workshops and trainings to improve individual and organisational competence at KEPA according to recommendations of the assessments. These assessments will be carried out by procured experts, either local, regional or Swedish depending on the nature of the issue. ToR will be developed by SEPA with input from KEPA. The current work plan is easy to follow, but does not provide a lot of detail. More specific baselines and targets for the activities will be presented in the inception report due in May 2021.

Documented Results - closing PM
Communication
Within the communication aspect, there has been clear results. For example, the communication outreach has worked well. Campaigns have been leading to a better outreach to the public, which have been able to be measured through social media tools. Moreover, clear results have been seen when it comes to knowledge on communication. The staff at KEPA have gotten increased knowledge of the importance of communication on social media. As an example of a result, an air pollution campaign was conducted, and increased the number of followers and interactions significantly. For example, on Facebook, the reach increased with 449.3%, showing the importance of good communication and what communication through social media can do/help achieve.
Environmental Information Systems, EIS
One of the main results achieved in the aspect is the creation of a metadata portal. The metadata portal makes it possible for the public to access the data and information from KEPA. This is an important result, as it is one of the EU requirements, and since Kosovo is aiming to access the EU, the portal is crucial for the agency. Connected to this is also the fact that a person that would manage this new system was recruted during the end of the project, to keep developing its function and maintain the result. This was also achieved through raising the KEPA team's awareness of the importance of a meta-data system. Specific workshops targeted this area so that more than one person could benefit from the portal, and concretly use it. Moreover, this also contributed to the capacity building of the KEPA team, as the civil servants not only increased their awareness of a well functioned IT-system, it is also enhanced their contribution to the internal and external methods to gather data to the portal. The ability to use EIS is not only a matter of having a digital platform, it is also linked to how to coordinate internally and externally to make the data flow efficient. A well functioned EIS means that the whole organisation should be at place, to gathering data and document it.
Water management
In the context of the water management, one of the first results achieved by SwEPA was that first-time data was developed for the Drini e Bardhe river. This contributed to enhanced knowledge at KEPA regarding what kind of pollution exists in the river, and it gave data for how the managing of the water pollution should be taken care of. It gave input to the long-term plan on how to remove the pharmaceutical contaminants from hospital waste water. Overall, the support in this context have helped lay a base and provide recommendations for continuous work with managing the water pollution and improve water quality in Kosovo.
Within this component KEPA was working closely with Dalarna County Administration Board, who is an expert Swedish Agency within this field.
Environmental quality improvement measures
In this context, the overall aim was to offer hands-on assistance for implementation while ensuring alignment with global standards. Moreover, through cooperation between KEPA and the Swedish Environmental Research Institute (IVL), studies were also carried out with much focus on air pollutants and emissions. The Greenhouse Gas and Air Pollution Interactions and Synergies (GAINS) model was used for doing the evaluation on this. Continuously, when the feasibility study was done a workshop was held and throughout the whole process of the study, several different stakeholders were involved which gave them more knowledge of the GAINS model. Overall, they gained more competence around what analytical and policy-making tools/instruments exist for addressing emissions, which helps them in the future with similar work and new studies.
National Parks
Under the National parks area, the main goal of this part of the project support was to promote socio-economic development and align the management of the parks with EU-standards and enhancing the governance.
The first very clear results are the cross-border cooperation between North Macedonia and Kosovo in the Sharri mountains. Through workshops and communication, the cooperation increased and there were many discussions on cooperation specifically when it comes to protection of the area and spatial planning. A second result was an increased competence regarding the EU Environmental legislation. This was done through an academy by SwEPA where people from the whole region's relevant agencies and organizations participated (they applied to attend the course).
Another accomplishment from the national park context is that a draft revised management plan for the Sharri National Park was done. Through this plan, input from stakeholders, new directives and experience form officials were taken into consideration, which made the management plan more relevant.
Other studies that were conducted, to lead the development of national parks (especially Sharri National Park), are the "Strategic Environmental Assessment Report for the Spatial Plan of Sharri National Park", conducted by UN-Habitat who earlier had done this job for the other national park: Bjeshket e Nemuna - in accordance with the law. This plan describes the current situation and the characteristics of the environment at the park. It also sketches out the possible future trends, how the environmental conditions impact the park and states out mitigation measures - finalizing with recommendations.
Parallel to this a socio-economic study of fees for national parks was performed. The Ministry of Environment, Spatial Planning and Infrastructure had specifically asked for this study with focus on fees, as part of strengthening the protection with for instance more guards. The study is - while writing this - now being used, enhancing the knowledge for KEPA-team on how fees can and other actions can benefit the parks.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
